1. 디모데후서\n 1) 바울의 마지막 유언과도 같은 서신\n - 디도서:
1. 2 Timothy
 1) A letter like Paul's last will and testament
 - At the end of Titus it looks like everyone except Timothy gathered at Nicopolis, but there's no record of them holding meetings, and a little later we see Paul locked up in the Mamertine Prison, Rome's prison for those condemned to death.
 - There was no hope of getting out, and when the thought came, ‘So in the end I'll be martyred,’ he missed Timothy terribly. That's why he wrote this letter. It truly is a letter like Paul's last will.
<딤후1:1~5> 디모데의 거짓 없는 믿음 때문에 눈물이 난다는 얘기: <2 Tim 1:1~5> He says Timothy's unfeigned faith brings him to tears
<딤후1:6~10> 우리 주의 증거와 또는 주를 위하여 갇힌 자 된 나:
<2 Tim 1:6~10>  Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God;
 - About the calling =>He called us not according to our works but by grace.
<딤후1:11~14>\n - 바울도 고난을 받았다고 이야기 한다.\n -:
<2 Tim 1:11~14>
 - Paul says he suffered too.
 - Faith, yes, but faith that works through love
<딤후1:15> 아시아에 있는 모든 사람이 나를 버린 이 일을 네가 아나:
<2 Tim 1:15> This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.
 -  Just as Jesus had Judas Iscariot.
- A man named Onesiphorus ->even when Paul was in prison, he wasn't ashamed, came often, and refreshed him.
<딤후2:1~2> 내 아들아 그러므로 네가 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 은혜:
<2 Tim 2:1~2> Thou therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
 - Passing on the teaching. I too am looking for faithful people to hand this Bible camp over to. I hope one of you will learn and carry this camp on.
 - Faithful people => believers
<딤후2:3~13> 또 고난 받으란 얘기. 내가 비록 갇히고, 매였으나: <2 Tim 2:3~13> Again, about enduring suffering. Though I'm imprisoned and in chains, the word of God is not bound.
<딤후2:14> 너는 저희로 이 일을 기억하게 하여 말다툼을 하지 말라고: <2 Tim 2:14> Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before God that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.
우리 애들에게 끊임없이 하는 말이예요. 쓸데 없는 것으로 말다툼 하지 말: This is what I tell my kids all the time. Don't quarrel over useless things. Quarreling ruins those who hear it.
<딤후2:15~19> 네가 진리의 말씀을 옳게 분변하여 부끄러울 것이 없: <2 Tim 2:15~19> Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
그렇지 않는 사람이 있는데 후메내오와 빌레도-> 부활이 이미 지나갔다: There are people who don't, Hymenaeus and Philetus-> saying that the resurrection is past already, and overthrow the faith of some.
<딤후2:20~26> 금그릇도 있고 놋 그릇도 있지만 하나님께서 쓰시는: <2 Tim 2:20~26> There are vessels of gold and vessels of brass, but the vessel God uses is a clean vessel.
22.네가 청년의 정욕을 피하고 주를 깨끗한 마음으로 부르는 자들과 함께: 22.Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes. And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; and that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, and be taken captive by God to do his will.
<딤후3:1~5> 네가 이것을 알라 말세에 고통하는 때가 이르리니 사람들:
<2 Tim 3:1~5> This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away.
 - The picture of the last days->exactly the same as the picture of today.
<딤후3:6~9> 항상 배우나 욕심에 이끌려 배우게 되면 진리에 이를: <2 Tim 3:6~9>  Ever learning, but if you learn driven by your own desires, you can never come to the truth.
<딤후3:10~12> 그리스도 예수 안에서 경건하게 살고자 하는 자는 핍: <2 Tim 3:10~12> All that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution
<딤후3:13~17> 성경은 능히 너로 하여금 그리스도 예수 안에 있는: <2 Tim 3:13~17> The scriptures are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
여기서 성경은 구약성경을 말함. 구약 성경이 예수 안에 있는 믿음으로 구: The scripture here means the Old Testament. It says the Old Testament leads to salvation through faith in Jesus.
<딤후4:1~5> 하나님 앞과 산 자와 죽은 자를 심판하실 그리스도 예수: <2 Tim 4:1~5> I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead, by his appearing and his kingdom; preach the word; be instant in season, out of season
<딤후4:6~8> 순교할 때가 된 것 같다는 얘기: <2 Tim 4:6~8> He says the time for his martyrdom seems to have come
그 다음엔 누구에게 문안하고, 가죽 종이에 쓴 책을 가져와라. 누가 좀:
After that it wraps up with things like: greet so-and-so, bring the books written on parchment, somebody find so-and-so and bring him.
 - Paul was martyred in 67, so it looks like he wrote this letter around the fall of 66. That's the kind of letter 2 Timothy is.
